picks.title: Eddie AI update: plan first, Resolve Studio panel, and more
picks.excerpt: Eddie AI now shows a plan before paid runs, adds a Resolve Studio panel and After Effects template import, plus 13 tool pages ahead of NAB Show New York.
picks.rationale: The AI editing assistant now shows its plan before spending paid credits and runs as a panel inside DaVinci Resolve Studio, so editors can use it in their existing Resolve workflow.

picks.title: My AXE Commercial Died in a Budget Meeting. Five Years Later, I Brought It Back with AI
picks.excerpt: Five years after budget constraints killed an ambitious AXE commercial, I finally resurrected it with AI. Here's how I approached AI filmmaking like a real production, and why I think these tools could change what's possible for independent filmmakers.
picks.rationale: A director describes, step by step, how she made a commercial that was cut for budget reasons using an AI pipeline run like a real production. Independent filmmakers can reuse her process.

picks.title: cinemaOS, CUTROOM, and invideo Compared – Mac Studio App, Free Open-Source Editor, Cloud AI Agent | CineD
picks.excerpt: cinemaOS, CUTROOM and invideo compared: a Mac studio app, a free open-source editor and a cloud AI agent editor.
picks.rationale: A side-by-side comparison of three different kinds of AI editing tool (a local Mac app, a free open-source editor and a cloud agent) helps editors pick one for their setup.

picks.title: Anime Studio Felix Film Edits Job Listing That Encouraged Generative AI
picks.excerpt: Japanese anime studio Felix Film revised a graduate animator job listing that had encouraged applicants to use generative AI, saying it has not decided to adopt generative AI for images but is studying its potential future use.
picks.rationale: After backlash, an anime studio rewrote a job listing that had encouraged new animators to use generative AI. The reversal shows how sensitive AI-skills hiring requirements still are in animation.

picks.title: Taika Waititi Says It’s “Probably Inevitable” AI Will Be Used in Hollywood But It’s “Boring and Lame” to “Type in Prompts to Make a Movie”
picks.excerpt: Waititi's new movie 'Klara and the Sun,' starring Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams, is set in a futuristic world with AI friends.
picks.rationale: A major director accepts that Hollywood will use AI but rejects prompt-driven filmmaking, a clear marker of where the line between AI as a tool and AI as the author is being drawn.
